issue.title: gui test red under load: provider-add-gemini.test webkit en 420px times out clicking #addProvider
issue.body:
`internal/gui/tests/provider-add-gemini.test.cjs`, `webkit en 420px: a custom provider with a Gemini URL alone is added`, went red once in a 66-file GUI run (`--test-concurrency=4`, machine load ~48 from other sessions' GUI runs), at origin/main 8299409e4 plus an unrelated app.js change (Providers nav dot for new partners):

```
not ok 184 - webkit en 420px: a custom provider with a Gemini URL alone is added
  duration_ms: 14052
  location: internal/gui/tests/provider-add-gemini.test.cjs:48:7
  error: locator.click: Timeout 5000ms exceeded.
    - waiting for locator('#addProvider')
    - locator resolved to <button ... id="addProvider">＋ Add provider</button>
    - attempting click action
    - waiting for element to be visible, enabled and stable
  stack: provider-add-gemini.test.cjs:58:44
```

`#addProvider` never became "stable" within the 5s default: at 420px the header is still settling (fitTop / layout moves) on a loaded machine. Alone it passes, and it passes on an origin/main 81a58d2f3 copy.

Likely fix: wait for the page's layout to settle (as other tests wait for the view's animations) before the click, or give this click the room the rest of the file has, rather than the 5s default.

comments.body:
The test fix is on [fix/r25-add-gemini-420px](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/r25-add-gemini-420px), commit 592958f9640e0c7651c55c33bb139130a67641b1.

The failing path is the first `#addProvider` click in `internal/gui/tests/provider-add-gemini.test.cjs`. Playwright's click waits for stable geometry over animation frames; WebKit's UI process can delay those frames and input under load. Duty-cycling only the test's own WebKit UI process reproduced a 5-second click timeout against clean-base assets, including the visible/enabled/stable call log. The app's handler is `internal/gui/assets/app.js` (`#addProvider.onclick` -> `unrollSheet`); there was no demonstrated Gemini URL handling defect.

The change uses a focused button's Enter activation through `reader.cjs:openAddSheet`, following the existing `openPart` approach. It retains trusted keyboard activation and the existing sheet-opening behavior. One new Linux WebKit test checks that the sheet and custom-provider entry open during the injected stall.

Validation: the affected Gemini scenario passed 20/20 (Chromium and WebKit, five languages, 1100px and 420px); the new stalled-frame test passed 1/1; the full Go `./internal/gui` suite passed. Go 1.26.8 vet and all three requested builds passed (native, Linux amd64 nogui, Windows amd64 cross-build).

RED -> GREEN qualification: the separate base click reproduction timed out and the new helper test passed at head. However, copying only the new test to a clean base fails with `openAddSheet is not a function`, rather than the reported timeout. That does **not** satisfy a strict behavioral regression RED requirement, so this branch is not a fully accepted delivery under that requirement.

Not tried: the original 66-file concurrent GUI workload, the entire 895-file browser suite, native Windows/macOS runtime behavior, or a real provider account. The new stall test uses Linux /proc and skips on other platforms. No application runtime code was changed and no upstream PR was opened.
